site.titleSuffix: Stream and record your DJI FPV goggles on a Raspberry Pi
site.description: Raspberry Pi 4 software that takes the live feed from DJI FPV goggles or a USB camera and sends it to HDMI, any browser, RTSP/SRT/RTMP/UDP streams and recordings.

footer.disclaimer: YStreamer is an independent open-source project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by DJI. DJI and its product names are trademarks of their respective owners.

hero.slogan: Your FPV feed, on every screen.
hero.subtitle: Software for a Raspberry Pi 4 that takes the live video from DJI goggles or a USB camera and sends it to an HDMI screen, to any browser, to streams and to recordings. Set up from a web interface.
hero.orInstall: Already running Raspberry Pi OS Lite? Install with one command:
hero.mediaAlt: The YStreamer web interface showing the live feed from the goggles

flow.title: Plug in the goggles. Send the video anywhere.
flow.subtitle: One Raspberry Pi in the middle, one cable from the goggles, and every output at once.

inputs.name: UVC Input
inputs.detail: DJI Action, OTG analog receivers, USB cameras and capture devices

outputs.name: Browser
outputs.detail: Live view on any phone or laptop

outputs.name: Recording
outputs.detail: To the SD card or a USB drive

features.title: Everything from the web interface
features.subtitle: Open the device in a browser and set it up there. No terminal needed.

items.title: Watch in the browser
items.text: Live view on any phone or laptop on the network, with WebRTC for the lowest latency.

items.title: Stream it out
items.text: An RTSP server, plus SRT, RTMP and UDP for OBS, ground stations and streaming platforms.

items.title: Record
items.text: To the SD card or a USB drive, by hand, automatically when video arrives, or with a physical button.

items.title: Air unit camera settings
items.text: Exposure, white balance, video format, colour profile and more, depending on the air unit.

items.title: Goggles status
items.text: The goggles' battery and the link quality, shown next to the video.

items.title: Logo and splash screen
items.text: Put your logo on the HDMI picture, and choose what shows while there's no video.

items.title: Remote access
items.text: Reach the device from anywhere through Tailscale or WireGuard.

items.title: Signed updates
items.text: Update from the web interface. If a new version doesn't start, the previous one comes back.

gallery.title: See it in action
gallery.subtitle: From the goggles to the big screen

compat.title: Works with your goggles
compat.subtitle: Connect the goggles to the Pi's USB-C port. The first DJI FPV Goggles and USB cameras go in a USB-A port.
compat.disclaimer: YStreamer is not affiliated with DJI.

install.title: Up and running in three steps

steps.title: Flash the image
steps.text: Write the ready-made image to a microSD card and put it in a Raspberry Pi 4.

steps.title: Plug in the goggles
steps.text: Connect them to the Pi's USB-C port with a data cable, and power the Pi on.

steps.title: Open ystreamer.local
steps.text: Join its YStreamer Wi-Fi or plug in Ethernet, then open it in any browser.

install.scriptHint: Already running Raspberry Pi OS Lite?

limits.title: Before you start
limits.subtitle: A few honest limits, so there are no surprises.

items.title: Raspberry Pi 4 only
items.text: YStreamer is tested only on the Raspberry Pi 4 Model B.

items.title: USB-C is for the goggles
items.text: While YStreamer is installed, the Pi's USB-C port is reserved for the goggles.

items.title: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, on purpose
items.text: Wi-Fi runs on 2.4 GHz only. 5 GHz interferes with the goggles' video link.

items.title: Lite, not desktop
items.text: Raspberry Pi OS with a desktop isn't supported: the desktop keeps the HDMI output. Use the Lite version.

cta.title: Put your FPV feed on the big screen
cta.text: Free and open source under GPL-3.0. Flash the image, plug in the goggles, open the browser.

download.heading: Download YStreamer
download.subtitle: Both ways end at the same place: the web interface at ystreamer.local.

image.title: Ready-made image
steps: Download ystreamer-<version>.img.xz (about 800 MB) from the latest release.
Write it to a microSD card with Raspberry Pi Imager ("Use custom") or balenaEtcher.
Put the card in the Pi, power it on and open http://ystreamer.local.
